question: Should OpenClaw accept identical repeated Content-Length values by introducing a transport path that normalizes raw response headers before Undici rejects them?
rationale: RFC semantics permit either rejection or normalization, while the current production Fetch stack deliberately rejects the response before this PR's code runs; changing that behavior crosses HTTP framing and SSRF-sensitive transport ownership.

options.title: Preserve Fetch rejection
options.body: Do not land the caller-only acceptance change; keep Undici's framing behavior unless a reachable non-Fetch case is demonstrated.

options.title: Sponsor guarded normalization
options.body: Implement narrowly scoped raw-header normalization with security-owner review and real transport tests for all affected paths.

recommendation.title: Preserve Fetch rejection
recommendation.body: Do not land the caller-only acceptance change; keep Undici's framing behavior unless a reachable non-Fetch case is demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared parser and the latest baseline across all three affected modules trace to their merged work.
